title: Massive 200GB GTA 5 Leak Reveals Scrapped Liberty City DLC and Early GTA 6 Files
description: A new 200GB GTA 5 data leak suggests Rockstar Games scrapped plans for a massive Liberty City DLC and includes very early GTA 6 development files.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Massive 200GB GTA 5 Leak Sheds Light on Scrapped Liberty City DLC and Early GTA 6 Work

According to a recent report by gaming outlet Eurogamer, Rockstar Games has been hit by a massive data leak involving a nearly 200GB version of GTA 5's source code and related files. This enormous data cache has sparked intense discussions across the gaming community, offering an unprecedented look into the inner workings of one of the industry's most secretive developers.

### A Liberty City DLC That Never Was

Among the files discovered in the massive 200GB leak are indications that Rockstar Games once started, and subsequently scrapped, plans for a massive Liberty City DLC for GTA 5. For years, fans have debated whether a single-player expansion for GTA 5 was ever in the works, much like the iconic Episodes from Liberty City in GTA 4. This leak strongly suggests that bringing Liberty City into the GTA 5 ecosystem was indeed on the drawing board at one point.

Industry observers and analysts suggest that the immense and sustained commercial success of GTA Online likely shifted Rockstar's development priorities away from single-player expansions, leading to the ultimate cancellation of the Liberty City project.

### Early GTA 6 Files Discovered

In addition to the remnants of the abandoned single-player content, the leaked data reportedly includes very early files related to GTA 6. As anticipation reaches a fever pitch for Rockstar's next major installment, any mention of early development files naturally draws immense attention. However, because these files date back to the very early stages of work, they likely represent preliminary concepts and foundational testing rather than finalized gameplay or features.

### Editor's Take

(Unconfirmed rumor) This massive 200GB leak offers a fascinating, if unauthorized, glimpse into the shifting priorities of game development at Rockstar Games. While discovering that a Liberty City DLC for GTA 5 was started and then scrapped is bittersweet, it highlights the difficult choices developers face. As for the early GTA 6 files, fans should exercise caution and wait for official communications from Rockstar rather than relying on unverified development scraps.
